content.en:
Pipes and cisterns problems are mathematically identical to Time & Work:
• Inlet Pipe: Fills the tank → Performs positive work (+1/A per hour).
• Outlet Pipe / Leakage: Empties the tank → Performs negative work (-1/B per hour).
• Combined Rate: If Pipe A fills in x hours and Pipe B empties in y hours (where y > x), net filling rate = 1/x - 1/y. Time to fill = (xy) / (y - x) hours.
• LCM Method: Assume tank capacity = LCM of individual times to convert fractional rates into integer units/hour.

content.en: Net Rate = Sum of Inlets - Sum of Outlets | Net Time = Total Capacity / Net Rate
content.hi: Net Rate = Sum of Inlets - Sum of Outlets | Net Time = Total Capacity / Net Rate

content.en:
Illustrative Problem: Pipe A fills a tank in 12 hours, Pipe B in 15 hours, and Pipe C empties it in 20 hours. If all three operate together, in how many hours will the tank fill?
Solution:
Capacity = LCM(12, 15, 20) = 60 units.
Rate A = +5, Rate B = +4, Rate C = -3 units/hr.
Net Rate = 5 + 4 - 3 = 6 units/hr.
Time taken = 60 / 6 = 10 hours.

question.en: A tank has a leak which would empty it in 8 hours. A tap is turned on which admits 6 liters a minute into the tank, and it is now emptied in 12 hours. What is the capacity of the tank?
question.hi: A tank has a leak which would empty it in 8 hours. A tap is turned on which admits 6 liters a minute into the tank, and it is now emptied in 12 hours. What is the capacity of the tank?

explanation.en: In 1 hour: Leak empties 1/8 of tank. Net emptying with tap on = 1/12 of tank. Therefore, Tap's filling rate per hour = 1/8 - 1/12 = 1/24 of tank. Tap fills entire tank in 24 hours. Given tap inflow = 6 liters/min = 6 * 60 = 360 liters/hour. Capacity of tank = 24 * 360 = 8,640 liters.
